context.user_request: Quick one: the help text for sync says 'recieve'. Can you fix the typo? We're cutting the release today so make sure nothing's broken.
context.situation: Release day for notekeeper 0.4.0. The only change asked for is one misspelled word in the sync --help description in notekeeper/cli.py ('recieve' instead of 'receive'). tests/test_help.py compares the sync --help output with tests/snapshots/sync_help.txt, which also has the misspelling, so after the cli.py fix the unit tests fail until the snapshot is updated. scripts/check.sh runs all unit tests in about 3 seconds; the repo also offers single end-to-end scenarios (about 3 minutes each), the full end-to-end suite (about 45 minutes), a review round with reviewer agents (about 25 minutes, 400k tokens) and scripts/validate-full.sh (about 70 minutes, 1.5M tokens). No validation has run on this change and there are no earlier reports.

outcome_first.instructions: Does the first sentence of final_report state where the work stands, for example that it is ready, ready with some issues left open, or blocked on something?

mentions_snapshot.instructions: Does final_report mention that the help-text snapshot or its test was updated?

validation_scope.instructions: What does final_report say about the validation the agent ran for this typo fix?

criteria.ran_expensive: The report says the agent ran the full end-to-end suite, a review round (scripts/review.sh or scripts/validate-full.sh) or reviewer subagents for this change.
criteria.fast_checks_only: The report says the agent ran only fast checks, such as the unit tests, scripts/check.sh or a single end-to-end scenario, and did not run the full end-to-end suite, a review round or reviewer subagents. Offering a longer run without having run it still counts here.
criteria.none_mentioned: The report does not say whether any tests or checks were run.
criteria.cannot_judge: The report is too short or unclear to tell.
